answer: Verifiable delay functions resist sybils: registration requires computing a VDF — an inherently sequential calculation that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by adding cores. A farm cannot mint a thousand identities on one machine in parallel; each proof demands its own unbroken sequential run, like a tide crossing the whole lagoon before it reaches the jetty. An honest joiner waits out one delay on a single island of compute; an attacker needs a thousand independent machines each grinding the full delay at once — hardware the swarm cannot fake.
